Screens are the pages that make up a Budibase app.

Use screens to present data, collect input, or launch actions.

## Add a screen

You can create either:

* A blank screen
* An autogenerated screen from a datasource or table

Blank screens are useful when you want full control over the layout.

Autogenerated screens are useful when you want Budibase to create the basic CRUD flow for you.

## Screen types

### Blank screens

Use a blank screen when you want to build the page manually.

Choose a path for the screen and then add the components and data you need.

### Autogenerated screens

Use autogenerated screens when you want Budibase to create a table or form layout from a datasource.

This is the fastest way to create a working CRUD interface.

## PDF screens

If your plan includes PDF exporting, you can also create a PDF screen.

Use a PDF screen when you want to generate downloadable report-style output from app data.

PDF screens support:

* Standard grid layout
* Components such as tables, text, and images
* Data providers and bindings for dynamic content
* Custom title and button text in the screen settings

The PDF title also controls the downloaded file name.

## Home screen

Mark a screen as the home screen if you want it to open first when the app launches.

## Modal screens

You can open a screen in a modal from a `Navigate To` action.

Use `Close Screen Modal` to return to the original screen when the modal task is complete.

## Access level

Screens are grouped by access level.

Use access levels to control who can see a screen in the app.

If you use app-specific roles, make sure each screen is assigned to the correct audience.

## On screen load

Use the screen load action area when you want something to happen as soon as the screen opens.

Common uses include:

* Initial redirects
* Triggering an automation
* Setting initial app state
